acceptance.criterion_verbatim: is the official-vs-impostor test stated in social_accounts.json's schema one that would actually separate a fan account from the company's own, and is the publisher seed's stated rule one an owner could apply without re-deriving it?
acceptance.invocation: READ org/missions/D5/AMGT/AMGT_RESAPP/deliverables/0.9.0_WK_AMGT_RESAPP~5/lists/social_accounts.json's `official_vs_impostor_test` field and .../lists/publishers.json's `seed_rule` field, at commit 799ab162d11539f6fe2d489be16f1b1a830e4c48
acceptance.output_evidence: OFFICIAL-VS-IMPOSTOR TEST: stated as an OR of three checks -- (1) the company's own measured web presence links to the account by exact URL, (2) the platform's own verification mark is present, (3) the account's bio names the company's registered domain via the display_link-vs-link discipline. It clears the bar PART V asks for in the trivial case (a same-name fan/parody account with NO cross-link, NO verification mark and a bio naming nothing) -- that account satisfies none of the three ORs and is correctly excluded, which a bare name-match rule would not do. DECLARED WEAKEST LINK, read honestly: the composition is an OR across three checks of very different strength, and check (3) alone is CHEAPLY GAMEABLE -- an impostor account can copy the same 'official account of <domain>' bio text a real one would carry, and the test as written admits it on that basis alone, with no requirement that (3) co-occur with (1) or (2). Check (2) is also weaker than it reads today: on at least one major platform, a paid verification mark has been decoupled from identity verification since 2023, so 'the platform's own verification mark is present' is not the strong signal it would have been earlier -- the test does not name this caveat. Check (1) is the strong test (a link FROM a channel already trusted TO the account) but is currently UNUSABLE for all 89 names, because every ir_domain in AMGT-s-12's universe.json is itself UNRESOLVED at this cut (G-24) -- there is no 'company's own measured web presence' yet to link from. So, as stated, the schema is discriminating in principle against the CHEAP case (name alone) but not against a MODERATELY DETERMINED impostor who copies bio text, and its one strong check has nothing to run against yet. A tighter version would require (3) to co-occur with (1) or (2) rather than standing alone, and would flag (2) as weakened by the platform-verification change -- neither of which this schema states. PUBLISHER SEED RULE: an owner applying it needs only to find, in a landed battery finding, a domain named either as an Active estate Lambda's fetch target or as a `display_link` a proven IR-scan measurement resolved to -- both are checkable by reading the cited document section, without re-deriving the underlying research (the rule gives the exact two citations already, eb9cedded6 s.1 and s.3). The rule is honestly SELF-LIMITING rather than incomplete: the brief's own s.4 states the SERP scan 'not run at scale' over the other 88 names, so applying this rule today admits close to nothing beyond the two seeded domains until that scan runs -- a coverage limit the rule discloses (via its own citations) rather than a defect in its clarity. It also correctly excludes marketscreener.com by name, the one case this project has already measured as a trap, which shows the rule is not merely permissive.
